title: Coalition negotiators to decide the fate of municipalities
gist: Oxford Economics expects South Africa's 4 Nov 2026 local elections to deliver further ANC decline without DA gains, producing fragmented hung councils where coalition negotiators decide outcomes, with implications for the national coalition and 2029.

insights.claim: The 2026 local government elections on November 4 are expected to be another chastening day for the ANC, whose support continues to plummet.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Further ANC erosion adds political uncertainty for South African assets.

insights.claim: Voters are not flocking to the DA; support is fragmenting, so the fate of many municipalities will be decided by party negotiators rather than voters.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Expect hung councils and unstable municipal governance, affecting service delivery and local credit.

insights.claim: Turnout is expected to be low as voters weary of petty politicking and dysfunctional coalitions ask whether their vote counts.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Low turnout raises uncertainty around result patterns.

insights.claim: The post-election window between results announcement and the first vote for mayor in council can change the election picture, with implications for the stability of the national coalition government and for the 2029 general election.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Watch coalition deals as a read-through to national political risk.
